name: Corfu
tagline: A lush Ionian island shaped by centuries of Venetian rule, its UNESCO-listed old town paired with some of Greece's greenest scenery and most striking coastline.
highlight: Corfu's Old Town, a well-preserved Venetian fortress town and UNESCO World Heritage Site, its architecture unlike anywhere else in Greece.
shortDescription: A lush Ionian island shaped by centuries of Venetian rule, its UNESCO-listed old town paired with striking coastline and green scenery.
metaDescription: A Corfu travel guide: the Old Town, the best beaches, when to go and a practical four-day itinerary.
knownFor: Corfu Old Town, its Venetian architecture, lush scenery

image.alt: Corfu's Old Town and its Venetian fortress above the harbour

intro: Corfu's history sets it apart from most of Greece — centuries of Venetian rule, followed by periods of French and British administration, left the island with a distinct architectural and cultural character, never having fallen under direct Ottoman control the way much of the mainland and other islands did.

That history is most visible in Corfu's Old Town, a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2007, its Venetian fortifications, Italianate architecture and the elegant Liston esplanade giving the island's capital an atmosphere unlike anywhere else in Greece.

Beyond the Old Town, Corfu is one of Greece's greenest islands, its interior covered in olive groves and cypress trees, with a coastline offering real range from dramatic cliffs to some of the country's most photographed beaches.

whyVisit.intro: Corfu's case is that no other Greek island combines this distinct a Venetian architectural heritage with this much genuine natural lushness.

points.title: The Old Town is unlike anywhere else in Greece
points.text: Centuries of Venetian, French and British influence produced a UNESCO-listed old town with a distinct character.

points.title: The island is one of Greece's greenest
points.text: Dense olive groves and cypress-covered hills set Corfu apart from the more arid landscapes of many other Greek islands.

points.title: The coastline offers real range
points.text: Dramatic cliffs, quiet coves and some of Greece's most photographed beaches all sit within a single island.

points.title: The food culture is distinctive
points.text: Venetian and Italian influence gives Corfu dishes found nowhere else in Greece, from pastitsada to sofrito.

points.title: It connects well to Italy and the wider Ionian
points.text: Ferries reach Italy directly, alongside easy connections to Paxos and other Ionian islands.

attractionsIntro: Corfu's essential sights, from its UNESCO-listed Venetian old town to its dramatic clifftop monastery and striking coastline.

attractions.name: Corfu Old Town

image.alt: An aerial view of Corfu's UNESCO-listed Old Town

attractions.text: A well-preserved UNESCO World Heritage Site, its narrow Venetian lanes, Italianate buildings and elegant Liston esplanade unlike anywhere else in Greece.
attractions.tip: Get lost in the old town's narrow kantounia lanes — much of its charm lies in unplanned wandering rather than a fixed route.

attractions.name: The Old Fortress

image.file: File:The Old Fortress and the Old Town of Corfu - September 2017.jpg
image.alt: The Old Fortress above Corfu's Old Town

attractions.text: An imposing Venetian, and later British, fortress on its own promontory, offering sweeping views across the old town and Ionian Sea.
attractions.tip: Visit late afternoon for softer light across the fortress walls and the sea beyond.

attractions.name: The New Fortress

image.alt: The New Venetian Fortress above Corfu's Old Town

attractions.text: A second, less-visited Venetian fortress above the old town, offering a quieter alternative view with real historic depth of its own.
attractions.tip: The New Fortress draws far fewer visitors than the Old Fortress — a good choice if you prefer avoiding crowds.

attractions.name: Achilleion Palace

image.alt: Achilleion Palace, built for Empress Elisabeth of Austria

attractions.text: A striking 19th-century palace built for Empress Elisabeth of Austria, its gardens and classical statuary reflecting her fascination with Greek mythology.
attractions.tip: The palace's gardens reward as much time as the interior — the statue of the dying Achilles is a particular highlight.

attractions.name: Paleokastritsa
attractions.text: A dramatic stretch of coastline on Corfu's west side, its turquoise coves backed by a clifftop monastery among the island's most photographed views.
attractions.tip: Boat trips from Paleokastritsa's beach reach secluded coves inaccessible by road.

attractions.name: Angelokastro

image.alt: The ruined Byzantine castle of Angelokastro on its clifftop

attractions.text: A ruined Byzantine castle on a dramatic clifftop above Paleokastritsa, one of the most important Byzantine fortifications in the Ionian Islands.
attractions.tip: The climb up is steep — reward yourself with the panoramic coastal views from the top.

thingsToDoIntro: Beyond the Old Town and its fortresses, Corfu rewards its beaches, its lush interior and its distinctive food culture.

thingsToDo.title: Wander the Old Town's kantounia lanes

image.alt: A narrow lane in Corfu's Old Town

thingsToDo.text: A rewarding way to experience Corfu's Venetian character, its narrow lanes hung with laundry lines opening onto small squares.
thingsToDo.tip: Morning light suits photography in the narrow lanes, before the day's heat and crowds build.

thingsToDo.title: Have a coffee on the Liston

image.alt: The arcaded Liston esplanade in Corfu Old Town

thingsToDo.text: Corfu Old Town's elegant arcaded esplanade, modelled on Paris's Rue de Rivoli, remains the island's classic spot to sit and watch the world go by.
thingsToDo.tip: The Liston gets busy in the evening — an earlier coffee offers a quieter, equally atmospheric experience.

thingsToDo.title: Swim at Paleokastritsa or a west coast beach

image.alt: The coastline and monastery at Paleokastritsa

thingsToDo.text: Corfu's west coast holds some of Greece's most striking turquoise coves, Paleokastritsa foremost among them.
thingsToDo.tip: Arrive early in peak season — Paleokastritsa's beaches fill quickly given their popularity.

thingsToDo.title: Take a boat trip to Paxos

image.file: File:Agion Apostolon church at Gaios of Paxos island Greece from far.jpg
image.alt: The harbour town of Gaios on the island of Paxos

thingsToDo.text: A worthwhile day trip to a smaller, quieter Ionian island, known for its own turquoise coves and traditional villages.
thingsToDo.tip: Boat trips typically include Antipaxos too — a beautiful smaller island with some of the Ionian's best beaches.

thingsToDo.title: Explore Corfu's olive groves and interior villages

image.alt: An olive grove in Corfu's lush interior

thingsToDo.text: The island's lush interior, covered in centuries-old olive groves, holds traditional villages well away from the coastal resorts.
thingsToDo.tip: A rental car rewards exploring the interior at your own pace, away from fixed tour routes.

thingsToDo.title: Try Corfu's distinctive Venetian-influenced cuisine
thingsToDo.text: Corfu's food culture is unlike the rest of Greece, its Venetian influence producing dishes found nowhere else in the country.
thingsToDo.tip: Look specifically for pastitsada or sofrito on taverna menus — both are distinctive to the island.

foodIntro: Corfu's centuries of Venetian rule left the island with the most distinctive food culture of any Greek island.

foods.name: Pastitsada

image.alt: Pastitsada, Corfu's signature tomato and pasta stew

foods.text: A rich tomato and spice-based stew of meat and pasta, Corfu's signature dish and unlike anything found on the mainland.
foods.whereToTry: Traditional tavernas throughout the Old Town and across the island.

foods.name: Sofrito
foods.text: Veal slow-cooked in a garlic and white wine sauce, a distinctive Corfiot dish reflecting the island's Venetian culinary heritage.
foods.whereToTry: Traditional tavernas across Corfu, particularly in the Old Town.

foods.name: Bourdeto
foods.text: A spicy fish stew in a rich red pepper sauce, one of Corfu's most distinctive seafood dishes.
foods.whereToTry: Taverns along the coast and in the Old Town, particularly those specialising in seafood.

foods.name: Corfu's kumquat products

image.alt: A bottle of Corfu's kumquat liqueur

foods.text: Kumquats, introduced to Corfu in the 19th century, are now a local specialty, turned into liqueur, spoon sweets and marmalade found nowhere else in Greece.
foods.whereToTry: Shops throughout the Old Town, many offering tastings of kumquat liqueur and preserves.

foods.name: Corfu olive oil
foods.text: Among Greece's most respected, reflecting the island's centuries-old, exceptionally dense olive groves.
foods.whereToTry: Local producers across the island, several offering direct tastings and sales.

foods.name: Tsitsibira ginger beer

image.alt: A bottle of tsitsibira, Corfu's traditional ginger beer

foods.text: A traditional Corfiot ginger beer, a legacy of the island's period of British administration, distinct from anywhere else in Greece.
foods.whereToTry: Cafes and shops throughout the Old Town, particularly around the Liston.

accommodation.intro: Corfu's right base depends on the balance you want between Old Town atmosphere and beach access.

areas.name: Corfu Old Town
areas.text: The island's most atmospheric base, putting the fortresses, Liston and Old Town restaurants all within easy reach.

areas.name: Paleokastritsa
areas.text: A striking coastal base, trading Old Town convenience for direct access to Corfu's most photographed coves.

areas.name: Kassiopi or the northeast coast
areas.text: Calmer resort towns offering direct beach access away from the Old Town's crowds.

gettingThere.intro: Corfu has its own international airport, with ferries also connecting the island to Italy and the mainland.

options.text: A short flight from [[athens|Athens]] reaches Corfu in about an hour, the fastest option from the Greek mainland.
options.detail: Book ahead in peak summer, when popular flight times can sell out or spike in price.

options.text: Direct ferries connect Corfu to Italian ports including Brindisi, Bari and Ancona, a popular route for travellers combining Greece and Italy.
options.detail: Overnight sailings from Italy offer a comfortable way to arrive without flying.

options.text: A short ferry from the mainland port of Igoumenitsa reaches Corfu in under an hour, useful for those driving from mainland Greece.
options.detail: Frequent daily crossings make this a flexible option without advance booking in most seasons.

gettingAround.intro: Corfu Old Town is walkable, with buses and rental vehicles covering the wider island.

options.text: The most practical way to reach Paleokastritsa, Angelokastro and the island's interior villages at your own pace.
options.detail: Coastal and mountain roads can be narrow and winding — allow more time than GPS estimates suggest.

options.text: A reasonably reliable network connects Corfu Town to the island's main beach towns and villages.
options.detail: Service to more remote interior villages is limited — a car helps for these areas.

options.text: A convenient option for Paxos and Antipaxos, which involve logistics easier left to a boat operator.
options.detail: Boat trips typically depart from Corfu Town or Paleokastritsa each morning in season.

bestTime.headline: May–June and September, for warm weather without peak crowds
bestTime.summary: Corfu's summer crowds and prices peak in July and August, and shoulder season offers comparable weather with real relief from both.

seasons.text: Mild, increasingly warm weather with the island's famous lush greenery at its most vivid.
Hot and reliably sunny, the best swimming weather, but also the island's most crowded and expensive months.
Warm sea temperatures lingering from summer, comfortable air temperatures and noticeably thinner crowds.
Wetter than much of Greece given the Ionian's climate, but mild and quiet, with the Old Town's architecture still rewarding a visit.

bestTime.avoid: Peak July and August without accommodation booked ahead — Corfu's popular beach towns fill considerably and prices spike.

itinerary.title: Four days in Corfu
itinerary.intro: The Old Town first, then the island's dramatic west coast, then its interior and a nearby island day trip.

days.title: Arrive in Corfu Town
days.morning: Land and settle into Corfu Old Town.
days.afternoon: The Old Fortress and the Liston.
days.evening: Dinner featuring pastitsada in the Old Town.

days.title: Paleokastritsa and Angelokastro
days.afternoon: Climb to the Byzantine castle of Angelokastro.
days.evening: Return to Corfu Town for dinner.

days.title: Achilleion Palace and the interior
days.summary: Imperial history and the island's lush countryside.
days.afternoon: Explore an interior village and Corfu's olive groves.
days.evening: A final Corfiot dinner featuring sofrito or bourdeto.

days.title: Paxos
days.summary: A day trip to a smaller, quieter island.
days.afternoon: Explore Paxos and, if included, Antipaxos's beaches.
days.evening: Return to Corfu Town for a final evening on the Liston.

tipsIntro: Practical notes on timing, transport and etiquette that make a real difference to a Corfu trip.
tips: Get lost in the Old Town's kantounia lanes — much of the charm lies in unplanned wandering.
Rent a car for at least part of the trip — Paleokastritsa, Angelokastro and the interior reward the flexibility.
Book accommodation ahead for peak summer, when Corfu's popular coastal towns fill up considerably.
Try pastitsada or sofrito at least once — both are distinctive to Corfu and found nowhere else in Greece.
Visit Paleokastritsa early in the day during peak season, before its beaches fill up.
Consider a ferry from Italy if combining Corfu with an Italian trip — the direct route is convenient.
Pack for more rain than other Greek islands if visiting in winter — Corfu's climate is noticeably wetter.

faq.q: How many days do you need in Corfu?
faq.a: Four to five for a first visit, enough to cover the Old Town, Paleokastritsa, Achilleion Palace and a Paxos day trip without feeling rushed.

faq.q: Is Corfu different from other Greek islands?
faq.a: Yes — centuries of Venetian rather than Ottoman rule gave Corfu a distinct architecture, food culture and overall atmosphere.

faq.q: Do I need a car in Corfu?
faq.a: Helpful but not essential — buses cover the Old Town and main beach towns reasonably well, though a car helps considerably for the interior and Angelokastro.

faq.q: What is the best time of year to visit?
faq.a: May to June and September offer warm weather with crowds and prices well below the July-August peak, which is the island's busiest season.

faq.q: Can I visit Italy from Corfu?
faq.a: Yes — direct ferries connect Corfu to Brindisi, Bari and Ancona, a popular route for travellers combining Greece and Italy.
